- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to lag or underreact to sentiment-driven rallies.
- Underestimate prices during negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.20) — model often fails to capture downside momentum or panic-driven drops.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — model tends to overcorrect or overreact to recent highs, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- Mean-reversion bias in medium-term forecasts — model frequently forecasts prices to revert to prior 10-15 day averages, missing sustained trends.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too low in early part of the horizon (first 5-7 days) — model underestimates initial momentum or sentiment-driven acceleration.
- Sentiment lag: model reacts to sentiment shifts with 2-3 day delay — adjust forecasts by adding 0.1–0.2 to forecast if sentiment turns positive within last 3 days.
- Avoid “flat” sentiment periods — if sentiment is near zero for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to underperform; apply a 0.05–0.10 upward bias to forecast.
